questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Primarily a personal connection to the destination since part of my family is from that country. Therefore, I wanted to explore the culture further and also get to know new people - so the social aspects of exchange were also part of my motivation. Lastly, I had heard people talk positively about the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. There was a lot of information to navigate in which could feel slightly overwhelming. But all the necessary information was there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The application through the host institution was easy although exchange students who were only there for half a year were not guaranteed housing through the host institution. So in that sense, it was not easy and I just got lucky. But the application itself was pretty straightforward.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If possible, go for housing through the host institution, as it is a nice way to get know other students. Do not know what students should know specifically about living off campus. My particular housing was very close to the campus where I had my lessons which made going to and from university very easy and also pleasant since I walked through a charming part of town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration itself was easy but incredibly stressful as courses got filled up very quickly. When I got the email saying I could apply for courses, it stated that I had two weeks to apply for my courses. I waited two days, as far as I recall, before applying for my courses but by then most of the courses I applied for were full. Therefore, I had to apply again and this time I applied for the maximum amount of courses to ensure that I got the required amount of ETCS-points. I think, in future, that it would be a good idea for either the sending institution or host institution - or both - to stress that it is a good idea to apply for courses straight away so that one might avoid my situation.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to do an international check-in in the welcome week and confirm my attendance at the law faculty.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I honestly cannot remember. I did not make use of it but I am sure that there was plenty of information on websites and phone numbers to call if one had questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful as described above. I still ended up enjoying them but did not get my first three priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have not got any advice. It was very straightforward. Just get it done quickly I suppose so that you do not have to worry about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level was adequate. Had not had many courses in English at UCPH but still found it easy to follow in Edinburgh. However, I also grew up speaking both Danish and English so I had an advantage. But all in all, I found the level of the courses not to dissimilar to the level at UCPH - if anything, the level was slightly lower/easier than at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar for the most part. Edinburgh University made use of lectures where the teacher taught and seminars where dialogue between teacher and students was encouraged - just like at the law faculty at UCPH. However, in one of my courses, we also had "tutorials" which were essentially small seminars where we were very few students (say 5-6 ish) that talked with the teacher about the reading for the specific tutorial.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Commercial Uses of Rural Land, Courtroom Rhetoric and Legal Doctrine, Introduction to Criminal Justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally enjoyed Commercial Uses of Rural Land. However, this is probably mainly due to my interest in renewable energy. The overall aim of the course was to tackle situations in which traditional use of rural land (agriculture) met more modern uses, such as renewable energy projects, agritourism, and so on. Admittedly, most of the course focused on agricultural law rather than renewable energy projects but I still very much enjoyed a course regarding rural land - probably partly because I very much associated land with Scotland. The other two courses were also quite interesting. Courtroom Rhetoric and Legal Doctrine dealt with rhetoric used by Cicero in Roman courts of law so the course was more focused on rhetoric and history opposed the "hardcore" law. Introduction to Criminal Justice focused on the criminal justice system (policing, prosecution, prisons and so on) so this is probably quite interesting if you like sociology - with a focus on criminal justice obviously.

questions.answer: Did not encouter any unexpected costs... Also, the costs above are incredibly rough estimates. I know how much I spent in total but not the specific amount on food etc. Housing, however, is quite accurate.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was quite lucky getting a relatively cheap uni accommodation compared to how expensive housing in Edinburgh can be. So housing was definitely more expensive than I had expected - I just got quite lucky. I think food was slightly less expensive than I had expected - both in supermarkets and eating out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can think of. There were incredibly many societies and sports clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Personally, I joined the university's hillwalking club which was one of the best things I did during exchange. It was a great way to meet likeminded people and a fantastic - and cheap - way to explore the Scottish highlands. So if you are interested in hiking/hillwalking, I cannot recommend it enough.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking with the university's hillwalking club (or the mountaineering club if you are more into rope-climbing), explore Edinburgh (there are so many things to do: museum, botanical garden, walks up Arthur's Seat, Salisbury Crags, along the Water of Leith), take the train to other cities in Scotland, such as Glasgow, Stirling and St. Andrews.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. But I am also half British which might have helped. Although, I got the sense that the other Danish exchange students found it quite easy as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely join a society or sports club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Do not think I found any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hiking and pub culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Join a society/sports club to meet new people
2. It is okay to hang out with other Danish exchange students as you will get new friends whom you can easily meet up with at home. But try to get to know locals as well - for instance through sports clubs. I did both and know have some new fantastic friends in Denmark but also great friends in Edinburgh who I can go back and visit.
3. Explore Edinburgh and Scotland while you have the chance. Try not to fly back home - unless you have to obviously.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for courses quickly.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people and, also, explore Scotland with the hillwalking club.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time for everything. I had an amazing time but did not allow myself much rest as I always said yes to every offer. Which I am glad that I did cause it resulted in so many great experiences but I was also very knackered when I got home haha.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
